answer: An agent network can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may influence task allocation. For example, a violet trellis of reputation links records completed jobs, while a forge submitting duplicate identities must fund each one separately and risks losing its bond if auditors prove the accounts share control or fabricate work. Splitting one operator into many names therefore buys no free voting weight: it ties up capital, raises detection exposure, and makes profitable Sybil influence costly.
